sentences: Population protocols compute through repeated interactions of finite-state agents.
Presburger arithmetic describes exactly the predicates expressible by these protocols, but equivalent representations can have very different sizes.
The question asks whether every arithmetic formula, including quantified ones, has a protocol with only polynomially many states in its formula length.
The source distinguishes existence of such a compact protocol from the complexity of constructing it.
The project studies representational succinctness at the interface between logical specifications and distributed computation.
